{
  "name": "workspaces",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "description": "Teaches agents that isolated per-agent checkouts exist in jj-colocated repos via `jjx` (jj's equivalent of a git worktree), and how to drive it: `jjx open <slug>` creates or idempotently resumes a managed sibling workspace and prints its path on stdout, `--from <revset>` bases it on an explicit revision instead of the caller's uncommitted state, `jjx open --unique <slug>` forces a fresh workspace for fan-out, `jjx add <path>` adds an existing checkout at an explicit path, and `jjx rm <path>` cleans up without discarding unsaved work. The single skill exists to be found by the failure it prevents — an agent about to conclude that parallel isolated work isn't possible in a jj repo, or reaching for a plain git worktree instead. A Claude Code mod shows which subagents work in which workspace: a pane grouped by workspace, opened by `/spaces` or when a subagent first lands in one, placing each agent from the `<repo>-spaces/<slug>` paths in its spawn prompt and its own tool calls.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Jacob Hoehler"
  },
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "keywords": [
    "jj",
    "jujutsu",
    "jjx",
    "worktree",
    "workspace",
    "parallel",
    "subagents",
    "isolation",
    "fan-out"
  ],
  "types": "./types/index.d.ts"
}
